bugs.title: Bus write failure crashes callers after DB commit succeeds
bugs.description: _publish_bus() is called AFTER the DB commit in update_status(), request_help(), and offer_help(). If _publish_bus() raises OSError (disk full, permission denied), the exception propagates to the caller. The DB state is already committed, but the caller sees an exception and may retry, creating duplicate DB entries. Or the caller aborts, thinking the operation failed when it actually succeeded.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Create HelpProtocol with bus_dir pointing to a read-only directory. 2. Call hp.update_status('working', 50.0, 'test'). 3. os.open() in _publish_bus raises PermissionError. 4. Caller sees exception even though team_status row was committed.
bugs.impact: Callers retry operations that already succeeded, creating duplicate help requests or work items. System state becomes inconsistent between what callers believe and what the DB contains.
bugs.fix:
Wrap every _publish_bus() call in try/except. In update_status (line 250), request_help (line 357), and offer_help (line 443), change from bare calls to guarded calls. Replace the _publish_bus method signature to catch internally:

    def _publish_bus(self, channel: str, msg_type: str, body: dict) -> Optional[str]:
        """Publish a message to the JSONL bus. Returns message ID or None."""
        import os
        import uuid as _uuid

        msg = {
            "id": str(_uuid.uuid4()),
            "type": msg_type,
            "channel": channel,
            "team": self.team,
            "agent_id": self.agent_id,
            "ts": time.time(),
            "ttl": 3600,
            "body": body,
        }
        raw = json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
        safe_ch = channel.replace("/", "_").replace("..", "_")
        filepath = os.path.join(self.bus_dir, f"{safe_ch}.jsonl")
        try:
            os.makedirs(self.bus_dir, exist_ok=True)
            fd = os.open(filepath, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
            try:
                os.write(fd, raw)
            finally:
                os.close(fd)
        except OSError as e:
            logger.error("Failed to publish bus message to %s: %s", filepath, e)
            return None
        return msg["id"]
bugs.test_needed: Test that update_status, request_help, and offer_help succeed (DB state committed) even when bus_dir is unwritable. Verify the returned values are correct and no exception propagates.

bugs.title: TOCTOU race in auto_assign_idle_teams: helper team status not verified inside transaction
bugs.description: auto_assign_idle_teams() calls get_idle_teams() (via find_compatible_helpers) outside the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, then inside the transaction it assigns the helper and sets their status to 'helping' WITHOUT checking that the team is still idle. Between the read and the write, the helper team may have changed status to 'working'. The UPDATE on line 661-668 overwrites the legitimate 'working' status with 'helping', corrupting the team's actual state.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Team B is idle. 2. Thread 1 calls auto_assign_idle_teams(), find_compatible_helpers returns Team B. 3. Before Thread 1's BEGIN IMMEDIATE, Team B calls update_status('working', ...). 4. Thread 1's BEGIN IMMEDIATE succeeds and overwrites Team B's status to 'helping'. 5. Team B is now marked as 'helping' while actually working on its own task.
bugs.impact: Helper team's legitimate work status is silently overwritten. The team is now assigned conflicting tasks. Work tracking is corrupted.
bugs.fix:
Inside the BEGIN IMMEDIATE block (after line 636), add a status check before assignment:

bugs.test_needed: Test: Team B is idle, auto_assign starts, Team B changes to 'working' before the BEGIN IMMEDIATE, verify auto_assign does NOT overwrite Team B's status. Team B should NOT be assigned.

bugs.title: Concurrent auto_assign_idle_teams double-assigns same helper to different requests
bugs.description: Two concurrent callers of auto_assign_idle_teams() each read the same idle teams. Each targets a DIFFERENT open request. Both succeed in their BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions because they lock on different request IDs. Both update the same helper team's status to 'helping', with the second overwriting the first. The helper team is now assigned to two requests but the DB only shows the last assignment.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Create 2 open help requests (R1, R2) and 1 idle team (Team B). 2. Two threads call auto_assign_idle_teams() simultaneously. 3. Thread 1 assigns Team B to R1, sets status='helping'. 4. Thread 2 assigns Team B to R2, overwrites status='helping'. 5. Team B is assigned to both R1 and R2 but its team_status only reflects R2.
bugs.impact: Double-assignment of work. One request's assignment is silently lost. Helper team's status is overwritten, losing the first assignment context.
bugs.fix: This is the same fix as BUG-HP-002 -- the status check inside the transaction prevents this. The helper_row check ensures the team is still idle/complete. After the first assignment sets the team to 'helping', the second assignment's check will find status='helping' (not in ('idle','complete')) and skip that team. See BUG-HP-002 fix code.
bugs.test_needed: Test: 2 open requests, 1 idle team, 2 concurrent auto_assign calls. Verify exactly 1 assignment total. The helper team should appear in exactly 1 assignment.

bugs.title: No status value validation -- any string accepted for team status
bugs.description: update_status() accepts any arbitrary string for the status parameter. The docstring says 'One of: idle, working, needs_help, helping, complete' but there is no enforcement. Invalid statuses like 'banana', '', or None will be stored. Teams with invalid statuses become invisible to get_idle_teams(), get_busy_teams(), and get_teams_needing_help(), effectively disappearing from the system.
bugs.reproduction: hp.update_status('INVALID', 50.0, 'task') -- stores 'INVALID' in DB. get_idle_teams() won't find it. get_busy_teams() won't find it. The team is invisible.
bugs.impact: Teams with typos in status values silently disappear from all queries. Debugging is extremely difficult since no error is raised.
bugs.test_needed: Test that update_status('banana', ...) raises ValueError. Test that update_status('idle', -5, ...) raises ValueError. Test that valid statuses still work.

bugs.title: fulfill_help has no authorization check -- any team can fulfill any request
bugs.description: fulfill_help() does not verify that (1) the request is in 'accepted' status, or (2) the calling team is the accepted helper (accepted_by_team == self.team). Any team can call fulfill_help() on any request in any state, including 'open' requests (marking them fulfilled without any work done) or requests accepted by a different team.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Team A creates request. Team B accepts it (offer_help). 2. Team C (unrelated) calls fulfill_help(request_id). 3. Request is marked 'fulfilled' and work item marked 'completed' even though Team C did nothing.
bugs.impact: Unauthorized completion of work. Work marked done without being done. Accepted team's work is preempted.
bugs.test_needed: Test that Team C calling fulfill_help on a request accepted by Team B raises ValueError. Test that fulfill_help on an 'open' request raises ValueError. Test that the accepted team can still fulfill normally.

bugs.title: No closed-state tracking -- operations after close() raise opaque ProgrammingError
bugs.description: close() calls self._conn.close() but sets no flag. Subsequent method calls use the closed connection and raise sqlite3.ProgrammingError('Cannot operate on a closed database.') which is confusing. In multi-threaded code, one thread can close() while another is between releasing self._lock and calling _publish_bus(), causing a race.
bugs.reproduction: hp = HelpProtocol(...); hp.close(); hp.add_work_item('test') raises ProgrammingError with no indication that close() was called.
bugs.impact: Confusing error messages. In multi-threaded scenarios, difficult-to-debug race conditions between close() and operations.
bugs.fix:
Add a _closed flag and check it in every public method:

    def __init__(self, db_path: str, bus_dir: str, team: str, agent_id: str) -> None:
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.bus_dir = bus_dir
        self.team = team
        self.agent_id = agent_id
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._closed = False
        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(
            db_path, timeout=30, check_same_thread=False,
        )
        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
        self._conn.executescript(_HELP_SCHEMA)
        self._conn.commit()

    def _check_closed(self) -> None:
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError(f"HelpProtocol instance for team {self.team!r} is closed")

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the database connection."""
        with self._lock:
            if not self._closed:
                self._closed = True
                self._conn.close()

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.close()
        return False

Then add self._check_closed() as the first line inside each public method's self._lock block.
bugs.test_needed: Test that calling any method after close() raises RuntimeError with clear message. Test that double-close does not raise. Test context manager usage (with HelpProtocol(...) as hp:).

bugs.title: offer_help allows self-help -- team can accept its own request
bugs.description: offer_help() does not check whether self.team matches the requesting_team of the help request. A team can call request_help() then offer_help() on its own request, winning the claim and assigning the work item to itself. Only auto_assign_idle_teams() has a self-assignment guard (line 614), but direct offer_help() does not.
bugs.reproduction: hp_a = HelpProtocol(..., team='team-a', ...); wid = hp_a.add_work_item('task'); rid = hp_a.request_help(wid, 'help'); hp_a.offer_help(rid) returns True. Team A is now helping itself.
bugs.impact: Team wastes resources 'helping itself'. The help request is consumed, preventing other teams from actually helping.
bugs.fix:
Inside offer_help(), after fetching the row (line 406-412), add a requesting_team check:

                row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT status, work_item_id, requesting_team FROM help_requests WHERE id = ?",
                    (request_id,),
                ).fetchone()

                if row is None or row["status"] != "open":
                    conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                    return False

                if row["requesting_team"] == self.team:
                    conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                    return False

Note: the SELECT must now also fetch requesting_team.
bugs.test_needed: Test that hp_a.offer_help(rid) returns False when hp_a is the requesting team. Verify the request remains 'open' after the rejected self-offer.

bugs.title: No zombie work item detection or recovery mechanism
bugs.description: When a helper team accepts a request (offer_help), the work item moves to 'in_progress'. If the helper crashes or never calls fulfill_help(), the work item is stuck in 'in_progress' forever and the help request is stuck in 'accepted'. There is no reaper, timeout, or recovery path. The stress tests (TestZombieWorkItems) confirm this scenario exists but the module provides no API to detect or recover from it.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Team A requests help. Team B accepts via offer_help(). 2. Team B's process crashes. 3. Work item is permanently 'in_progress'. Help request is permanently 'accepted'. No other team can pick it up.
bugs.impact: Work items are permanently stuck. The requesting team cannot get help from anyone else. System liveness is compromised.
bugs.fix:
Add a reaper method to HelpProtocol:

    @_retry_on_busy
    def reap_stale_assignments(self, timeout_seconds: float = 300.0) -> list[dict]:
        """Find and reset help requests accepted more than timeout_seconds ago
        but never fulfilled. Returns list of reopened requests."""
        cutoff = time.time() - timeout_seconds
        reopened = []
        with self._lock:
            rows = self._conn.execute(
                """SELECT hr.id as request_id, hr.work_item_id, hr.accepted_by_team
                   FROM help_requests hr
                   LEFT JOIN team_status ts ON hr.accepted_by_team = ts.team
                   WHERE hr.status = 'accepted'
                     AND hr.resolved_at IS NULL
                     AND (ts.last_updated < ? OR ts.team IS NULL)""",
                (cutoff,),
            ).fetchall()

            now = time.time()
            for row in rows:
                self._conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE help_requests SET status = 'open', accepted_by_team = NULL, accepted_by_agent = NULL WHERE id = ?",
                    (row["request_id"],),
                )
                if row["work_item_id"] is not None:
                    self._conn.execute(
                        "UPDATE work_items SET status = 'available_for_help', assigned_to = NULL, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
                        (now, row["work_item_id"]),
                    )
                reopened.append(dict(row))

            if reopened:
                self._conn.commit()
        return reopened
bugs.test_needed: Test: Team B accepts request, simulate stale team_status (last_updated old), call reap_stale_assignments, verify request is reopened to 'open' and work item reset to 'available_for_help'. Verify a new team can now offer_help on the reopened request.

bugs.title: Empty list [] for required_caps treated as None due to Python falsy evaluation
bugs.description: In add_work_item(), line 273: `caps_json = json.dumps(required_caps) if required_caps else None`. Since empty list [] is falsy in Python, passing required_caps=[] stores None instead of '[]'. This makes it impossible to distinguish between 'no capabilities specified' (None) and 'explicitly requires no special capabilities' ([]). When find_compatible_helpers reads this back, both cases are treated as 'no specific capabilities needed -- all idle teams are compatible', which is correct for [] but may not be the intended behavior for the caller.
bugs.reproduction: hp.add_work_item('task', required_caps=[]) stores NULL in required_capabilities. hp.add_work_item('task', required_caps=None) also stores NULL. The two are indistinguishable.
bugs.impact: Loss of semantic distinction. Minor in practice since the downstream behavior (all teams compatible) is the same for both cases, but it's a data fidelity issue that could matter for future features like capability auditing.
bugs.fix:
Change line 273 to check for None explicitly:

        caps_json = json.dumps(required_caps) if required_caps is not None else None
bugs.test_needed: Test that add_work_item(required_caps=[]) stores '[]' in the DB, not NULL. Test that add_work_item(required_caps=None) still stores NULL.

bugs.title: request_help does not validate work_item_id existence or ownership
bugs.description: request_help() fetches required_capabilities from the work item (line 332-337) but does not verify the work item exists or belongs to self.team. If work_item_id is invalid, row is None, caps is None, est is None, and the method silently creates a help request for a nonexistent work item. It also runs an UPDATE on the nonexistent item (no-op). If the work item belongs to another team, request_help modifies it without authorization.
bugs.reproduction: hp_a.request_help(99999, 'help me') -- creates a help request referencing nonexistent work item 99999. hp_a.request_help(team_b_work_id, 'help') -- changes Team B's work item to 'available_for_help' without authorization.
bugs.impact: Orphaned help requests pointing to nonexistent work items. Cross-team work item status corruption.
bugs.test_needed: Test that request_help with nonexistent work_item_id raises ValueError. Test that Team A cannot request_help on Team B's work item. Test that valid work items still work.

bugs.title: complete_work_item has no ownership check -- any team can complete any work item
bugs.description: complete_work_item() updates any work item by ID without checking if self.team is the owner or the assigned helper. Any team can mark any other team's work item as completed.
bugs.reproduction: Team A creates work item 1. Team B calls hp_b.complete_work_item(1) -- succeeds, marking Team A's item completed without authorization.
bugs.impact: Work items can be prematurely or falsely marked as completed by unauthorized teams.
bugs.fix:
Add an ownership or assignment check:

    @_retry_on_busy
    def complete_work_item(self, work_item_id: int) -> None:
        """Mark a work item as completed."""
        now = time.time()
        with self._lock:
            row = self._conn.execute(
                "SELECT team, assigned_to FROM work_items WHERE id = ?",
                (work_item_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Work item {work_item_id} does not exist")
            # Allow completion by owner team or assigned helper
            is_owner = row["team"] == self.team
            is_assignee = row["assigned_to"] is not None and self.agent_id in row["assigned_to"]
            if not is_owner and not is_assignee:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Team {self.team!r} is not authorized to complete work item {work_item_id}"
                )
            self._conn.execute(
                "UPDATE work_items SET status = 'completed', updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
                (now, work_item_id),
            )
            self._conn.commit()
bugs.test_needed: Test that Team B cannot complete Team A's unassigned work item. Test that Team A can complete its own work item. Test that the assigned helper can complete the work item.

bugs.title: No priority validation in add_work_item -- invalid priorities break help request ordering
bugs.description: add_work_item() accepts any string for priority. The CASE expression in get_open_help_requests() (lines 379-384) only handles 'critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low'. Invalid priorities fall through to ELSE (value 4), sorting below 'low'. This is technically functional but means a typo like 'hgih' silently demotes the work item to lowest priority.
bugs.reproduction: hp.add_work_item('urgent', priority='critcal') -- typo stored in DB. Help request sorts at priority 4 (below 'low') instead of priority 0.
bugs.impact: Silent priority demotion from typos. No feedback to the caller that the priority is invalid.
bugs.test_needed: Test that add_work_item(priority='invalid') raises ValueError. Test that add_work_item(title='') raises ValueError. Test that valid priorities still work.

bugs.title: auto_assign_idle_teams falls back to any idle team even when required_caps are specified
bugs.description: When find_compatible_helpers() returns no matches (no idle team has any required capability), auto_assign_idle_teams() falls back to assigning ANY idle team (line 608-609: helpers = self.get_idle_teams()). This means a help request requiring 'ml' expertise could be assigned to a team with only 'design' capability. The capability matching is effectively advisory-only with an unrestricted fallback.
bugs.reproduction: 1. Help request requires ['ml', 'data-science']. 2. Only idle team has capabilities ['design', 'css']. 3. find_compatible_helpers returns []. 4. Fallback assigns the design team to an ML task.
bugs.impact: Teams assigned to tasks they lack capabilities for. Wasted effort and potentially incorrect work output.
bugs.test_needed: Test that a help request with required_caps=['ml'] is NOT assigned to a team without 'ml' capability when no matching teams exist. Test that requests with no required_caps still get the fallback.

bugs.title: _retry_on_busy decorator does not preserve function metadata (functools.wraps missing)
bugs.description: The _retry_on_busy decorator returns a bare wrapper function without @functools.wraps(func). This means all decorated methods lose their __name__, __doc__, and __module__ attributes. Logging on line 93 correctly uses func.__name__, but introspection, help(), and debugging tools show 'wrapper' instead of the actual method name.
bugs.reproduction: hp = HelpProtocol(...); print(hp.update_status.__name__) outputs 'wrapper' instead of 'update_status'. help(hp.update_status) shows no docstring.
bugs.impact: Poor debugging experience. Logging and stack traces show 'wrapper' instead of actual method names.
bugs.test_needed: Test that hp.update_status.__name__ == 'update_status' and hp.update_status.__doc__ is not None.
